evals.name: smart-fridge-reorder
evals.prompt: We're designing a 'smart fridge' feature for a grocery delivery app that tracks what users eat, predicts when they'll run out, and auto-suggests reorders. Run the Inverted Behavior Model — what behaviors will this actually trigger beyond convenient reordering?
evals.expected_output: Behavior model mapping intended behaviors (convenient reordering) and unintended behaviors (overconsumption, food waste, anxiety about being tracked, dependency) with likelihood and severity.

evals.name: productivity-gamification
evals.prompt: Our enterprise tool gamifies work — it awards points for tasks completed, displays team leaderboards, and gives badges for 'deep focus' sessions. Apply the Inverted Behavior Model: what behaviors are we actually motivating beyond productivity?
evals.expected_output: Model showing how gamification triggers task-splitting, performative busyness, competition anxiety, and focus-session gaming, alongside the intended productivity gains.

evals.name: social-savings-feature
evals.prompt: Our banking app lets users create shared savings goals with friends (e.g., 'Trip to Japan fund') where everyone can see contributions. Run the Inverted Behavior Model on this social savings feature.
evals.expected_output: Behavior model covering intended (motivation to save) and unintended behaviors (social pressure, shame, financial exposure, relationship strain) with severity mapping.
